did: Rust Rounds' week became a set of decisions. The new week format lands every ticket's speak-to points as forks, each a few honest options with one recommended, every option citing the week's stated constraints, and each ticket carries an academy of scratchpad exercises. The phone reads both the old and new weeks, home's mailbox takes the new one and home's server learns to read it, the time tracked on a week is kept at home and leaves with the account, and the phone now has the logic that keeps every pick at a fork and every step done or skipped, never rewritten. The screens that use it are next.

calls.title: How big a new-format week may be
options: Keep the old 32 KiB ceiling for every week
Allow 128 KiB for a new-format week, checked where the routine writes it
calls.why: A full week with forks and an academy is about 106 KB, so 32 KiB refuses every real one; the ceiling sits only where the week is written, since reading it back can change its bytes.
calls.undo: Lower WEEK_V2_MAX_BYTES in week-check and the routine refuses bigger weeks again (C700).

calls.title: Stop before the phone screens
options: Build the screens in this session
Stop after the logic and hand the screens to a fresh session
calls.why: This session had already run long once; the screens touch the most code, and a fresh session with the written plan on #3249 builds them more reliably.
calls.undo: Pick the screens up in any session from the plan on #3249.

left: The routine still writes the old week format: it switches once home's server serves the new one, and first the essay must take 1 to 6 points or the routine must hold to 2 or 3 forks (#3257).
The phone screens for read, academy, voice and each decision are planned on #3249, not built.
Sending each decision home needs a server field, written as a handoff patch for the coordinator.
The work tracker's runtime, its home client and the week visual are not built (#3250).
